space: fsaverage6, millimetres, origin centred, the same space as vessels.json and the cortical mesh
caption: Schematic pathways from standard neuroanatomy. Not patient-specific.
note: These are hand placed centrelines showing where each transmitter system runs, drawn from textbook neuroanatomy. They are not tractography, they are not derived from this patient, and they are not derived from any scan. Each one starts at its source nucleus and ends in the territory it projects to. The source nuclei are brainstem and basal forebrain structures that sit below the cortical surface, so the first point of a pathway is usually inside the brain rather than on the mesh.

pathways.name: Dorsal raphe to cortex
pathways.about: The dorsal raphe sits in the midline of the brainstem and sends serotonin fibres forward along the medial forebrain bundle to almost the whole cortex.

pathways.name: Median raphe to limbic system
pathways.about: The median raphe projects to the hippocampus and the limbic structures either side of the midline.

pathways.name: Raphe to striatum
pathways.about: A branch of the same ascending serotonin system that ends in the striatum.

pathways.name: VTA to nucleus accumbens
pathways.about: The mesolimbic pathway. The ventral tegmental area sits in the midbrain and projects forward to the nucleus accumbens.

pathways.name: VTA to prefrontal cortex
pathways.about: The mesocortical pathway. The same midbrain source, carried forward to the prefrontal cortex.

pathways.name: Substantia nigra to striatum
pathways.about: The nigrostriatal pathway, the one that fails in Parkinson's disease. It runs from the substantia nigra up into the putamen and caudate.

pathways.name: Locus coeruleus to cortex
pathways.about: A small nucleus in the dorsal pons whose fibres reach almost the entire cortex. It is the brain's main source of noradrenaline.

pathways.name: Locus coeruleus to hippocampus
pathways.about: The branch of the same system that reaches the hippocampus.

pathways.name: Locus coeruleus to thalamus
pathways.about: The branch that ends in the thalamus, which is part of how noradrenaline changes arousal.

pathways.name: Basal forebrain to cortex
pathways.about: The nucleus basalis of Meynert sits under the front of the brain and supplies acetylcholine to the whole cortex. It is the system lost early in Alzheimer's disease.

pathways.name: Medial septum to hippocampus
pathways.about: The septohippocampal pathway, which runs back through the fornix and sets the hippocampal theta rhythm.

pathways.name: Tuberomammillary nucleus to cortex
pathways.about: The only source of histamine in the brain, in the posterior hypothalamus. It projects widely and is part of staying awake, which is why antihistamines are sedating.
